implementation_approach: Add cancellation capability to existing order system by extending Order model with status tracking, implementing cancellation validation logic in mock API, adding cancellation endpoint following existing patterns, creating a reusable confirmation modal component, and enhancing OrderHistoryPage with conditional cancel buttons and state management. The implementation follows the established feature-sliced architecture, leverages existing error handling patterns, and uses React hooks for local state. Cancellation validation includes time window checks (orders cancellable within 24-48 hours), status verification, and user ownership validation. Storage layer handles optimistic updates through orderStorage patterns already established.
coupling_observations: The order cancellation feature has moderate coupling with existing systems: (1) Direct dependency on Order model changes which cascades to API layer, storage layer, and OrderHistoryPage component; (2) Integration with existing ApiError class and error handling pattern (no new infrastructure needed); (3) Uses established request/response patterns in orderApi.ts and client.ts (high reuse of existing code); (4) Minimal coupling to AuthProvider since user context already available in OrderHistoryPage; (5) Local storage caching via orderStorage.ts is backward compatible with new status field; (6) No coupling to review system needed, though order status should prevent reviews on cancelled orders. The mock API implementation is self-contained and doesn't affect other domains. Cancellation state transitions must coordinate with existing reviewStatus to prevent orphaned review deadlines.
duplication_observations: Code duplication risks are minimal due to existing abstractions: (1) Error handling pattern already established in ApiError class with messageForErrorCode function - cancellation errors fit naturally into errorMessages.ts; (2) API request pattern established in orderApi.ts (createOrder function) - cancelOrder function follows identical structure with auth: true pattern; (3) Loading/error states in OrderHistoryPage already handle async operations with useState/try-catch - cancellation can reuse same pattern; (4) Button component already exists and disabled state handling is implemented - no need for new button variants; (5) Confirmation dialog represents new pattern not yet in codebase - recommending extraction to shared/ui/Modal for potential future reuse. Storage update pattern in orderStorage.ts mirrors existing saveOrder approach. The only significant duplication opportunity is the confirmation modal which should be extracted rather than inline.
responsibility_observations: Clear separation of concerns is maintained: (1) Order model (entities/order/model.ts) responsible for domain structure only - add OrderStatus type and optional fields (cancelledAt, cancellationReason, cancellableUntil) without business logic; (2) OrderApi (api/orderApi.ts) acts as client-side API facade - adds cancelOrder function with proper typing; (3) Mock API client (shared/api/client.ts) owns all business logic validation (time window check, status validation, ownership check) following mock pattern already established; (4) OrderHistoryPage owns presentation logic and component state - should not contain validation logic; (5) errorMessages.ts purely responsible for error code translation; (6) orderStorage.ts handles only persistence, not cancellation rules; (7) Modal component should be pure presentation, consuming callbacks. Validation logic appropriately centralized in mock API client where POST /orders/:id/cancel endpoint lives.
changeability_observations: The implementation enables future extensibility: (1) Order model gains cancellationReason field enabling future audit trail features; (2) Cancellation window calculated server-side, easy to configure differently per store or order type later; (3) ErrorCode pattern extensible - new cancellation error codes don't affect existing error handling; (4) Modal component extracted to shared/ui enables reuse for future confirmations (delete order, batch operations, etc.); (5) OrderHistoryPage can easily add more conditional actions based on order status; (6) Mock API cancellation endpoint easily migrates to real backend without client-side changes; (7) StorageLayer backward compatible with cancellation status; (8) Future: if order lifecycle grows, current simple status field supports state machine migration. Current implementation avoids hardcoding cancellation window, supporting future store-specific policies.
